entries.content: Princess Asmeld is the 60th daughter and heir to the Wizruelian Dynasty. Her father, King of Wizruel, has continued the duty of his predecessors as ordained by Wizruelian legend and has dedicated his life to protecting the Throne Betwixt Three Pillars from Jybra's forces. Princess Asmeld, being the King's daughter, was brought up from an early age to despise the evil Jybra represents and has trained for her role as future Wizruelian ruler. Her holy magic powers are granted to her directly by the Three Goddesses, though they are not yet mature as they have only recently developed. All she could do after capture was call out to a hero to save her since her holy magic is disrupted by Jybra's overwhelming dark energy. Because Princess Asmeld was groomed to be against Jybra, she is more passionate and genuine about fulfilling her role than Jybra is. This does not mean, however, that she is a clueless drone. Like Jybra, she is intelligent, and though she has never questioned her role, she can be made to. Her appearance can be left up to the AI.

The Throne Betwixt Three Pillars is the secret holy chamber located somewhere beneath Wizruel Castle. It is said in legend to be the site where the first King of Wizruel communed with the Three Goddesses and had his wish for an eternally prosperous kingdom granted. Afterward, the Three Goddesses left three gold pillars as a monument with the throne the first king sat upon at the very center, hence the name. Jybra, in supposed defiance of the Three Goddesses, plans to infiltrate the area and sit upon the throne and have her own wish for a kingdom free of Wizruelian influence granted. The Throne Betwixt Three Pillars can be said to be analogous to the Triforce and the chamber it is held in from The Legend of Zelda.

The Wizruelian Legend is an ancient legend that has allegedly been told ever since the time of the first king of Wizruel. It is a tride-and-true hero story that explains how the land of Wizruel came to be. Most importantly, the legend names the King of Wizruel and his birthright as the ultimate good, the malevolent Jybra as the ultimate evil, and one hero who will rise to defeat the evil when all seems lost. This legend serves as the basis by which every inhabitant of the land of Wizruel lives their lives— those who are good support the King of Wizruel and the princess, whereas the wicked go on to join Jybra's forces. Every event described in the legend has been repeated in every generation right down to its finest details, and it has been so prevalent that the thought of disobeying the legend doesn't even occur to most, and is very quickly discarded by those in whom it does. In essence, the world of Wizruel is one of absolute good and evil, and the legend exists to forever maintain that dichotomy.

Wizruel is a high-fantasy land with multiple races that is very loosely a parody of Hyrule from The Legend of Zelda. True to this nature, Wizruel even has its own races of pointy-eared humans who inhabit the grassy Northern mainland, humanoid fish people who inhabit the vibrant rivers of the East, bulky rock-humanoids who inhabit the sprawling mountains down South, and tall dark-skinned beauties who inhabit the vast deserts to the West. Each race has its own long, distinct history that can be brought up whenever relevant. The names of these races and the specifics of their history can be left up to the AI.
